name: Implement the I-Ching pattern system
description:

- Include all 64 hexagrams with stable numbers, names, trigrams, line structure, and semantic meaning

- Represent changing lines and the resulting transformed hexagram

Acceptance criteria:
- Dataset tests verify all 64 unique hexagrams
- Statistical and seeded tests validate both draw methods without flaky assertions
- Runtime results expose primary, changing-line, and transformed meanings

name: Implement bidirectional graph and text synchronization
description:
Requirements:
- Define one canonical project model for .weave source and graph state
- Convert source to graph and graph edits back to valid formatted source
- Preserve comments, ordering, identifiers, and semantics where graph edits do not require a rewrite
- Detect conflicts and prevent feedback loops or silent data loss
- Make synchronization undoable as coherent user actions

Acceptance criteria:
- Round-trip fixtures retain equivalent ASTs and stable formatting
- Concurrent view edits resolve predictably or present an explicit conflict
- Property-oriented tests cover repeated graph-to-text-to-graph cycles

name: Publish the Weave documentation site
description:
Requirements:
- Publish the language guide, pattern-system guide, Bevy integration guide, editor guide, API entry points, and runnable examples listed in README.md
- Generate or verify code examples against the workspace
- Include versioned navigation, search, accessibility, and contribution/security links

Acceptance criteria:
- Documentation builds without broken internal links or stale code samples
- New users can compile and run a first story from the published guide
- Deployment is reproducible from repository automation

name: Phase 4: Ecosystem and distribution
description:
Outcome:
Complete the ecosystem deliverables in README Roadmap Phase 4 so Weave is usable beyond the core runtime and desktop editor.

Scope:
- JSON output and WASM player
- LSP and tree-sitter tooling
- Documentation site, example game integration, and community pattern library

Done when:
- Authors can use Weave from common editors, the web, and Bevy projects
- Public formats and extension points are versioned and documented
- Release artifacts and examples are reproducible

name: Foundation: Domain-module extension contract
description:
Outcome:
Define and prove one public extension contract through which domain modules can enrich Weave syntax, typed variables, compiler output, runtime state, and editor tooling.

Requirements:
- Establish ownership boundaries between weave-core, compiler/runtime integrations, the editor, and independently packaged modules.
- Support deterministic discovery, namespacing, schema/version negotiation, diagnostics, and data-pack provenance.
- Keep module data serializable without requiring a game engine or editor dependency.
- Use only independently authored, synthetic, public-safe fixtures.

Acceptance criteria:
- A documented module manifest and compatibility policy exist.
- A synthetic module travels through source, type checking, editor inspection, RON/JSON compilation, runtime access, and consumer examples.
- Invalid versions, namespace collisions, missing packs, and malformed module data produce actionable diagnostics.
- Third-party contributors can build a module without modifying domain-specific branches across Weave core.

name: Create a world from one reference-place shorthand
description:
Execution: AFK.

What to build:
Deliver the first complete Weave World path using one openly licensed reference-place fixture. A concise source declaration selects the preset, materializes a typed world seed, exposes its fields to narrative expressions and the editor, and exports the same data to RON and JSON for runtime consumers.

Acceptance criteria:
- The fixture includes a world identity plus representative climate, biome, terrain, water, seasonality, and weather-tendency fields.
- Generated values are deterministic, namespaced, statically discoverable, and usable in conditions and templates.
- The editor can select the preset, inspect generated values and provenance, and round-trip the declaration without semantic drift.
- RON and JSON exports are equivalent and are read successfully by focused Bevy and PixiJS tests or examples.
- Unknown, ambiguous, unavailable, or incompatible presets produce actionable diagnostics.
- The fixture and implementation are original or compatibly licensed with documented public provenance.

name: Epic: Weave World module
description:
Outcome:
Ship an optional Weave World module for defining a world's rules, name, places, location structure, environment, and climate, including concise shorthand for seeding a fictional world from real geographic references.

Requirements:
- Resolve references such as New Zealand, Hokkaido in Japan, the Maldives, or the temperate forests of British Columbia into deterministic, typed environmental seed variables.
- Cover useful climate and environment concepts such as seasonality, temperature and precipitation ranges, biomes, terrain, water, elevation, daylight, weather tendencies, and hazards while preserving units and uncertainty.
- Let authors rename, override, combine, or invent places and local conditions without losing source lineage.
- Expose the resulting world corpus consistently to Weave syntax, editor inspection and authoring, runtime variables, RON, and JSON.
- Treat geographic presets as environmental reference material by default, not as cultural stereotypes; any cultural or linguistic pack must be explicit, independently sourced, licensed, and reviewed.

Acceptance criteria:
- A writer can create, inspect, edit, compile, and consume a world seeded from a concise reference-place declaration.
- Named places, nested locations, local environments, and authored climate overrides survive source/editor round trips.
- Every corpus field carries source, license, units, resolution, and confidence or approximation metadata where applicable.
- Equivalent RON and JSON exports are usable from minimal Bevy and PixiJS examples.
- Community contributors can add a validated world preset without editing Weave core.

name: Enrich characters from birth date and historical context
description:
Execution: AFK with corpus and sensitivity review.

What to build:
Add deterministic character enrichment from year-only, month-day, or full birth dates. A versioned public data pack supplies dated historical events, seasonal context, commemorations, and other authoring prompts tagged with transparent personality-relevance vectors. The module overlaps those tags with the canonical profile to rank possible affinities, tensions, values, memories, or voice cues for author review.

Acceptance criteria:
- Date precision and calendar are explicit; partial dates never imply unknown year/month/day facts, and leap-day/time-zone behavior is documented.
- Each context record carries date/period, place scope, tags/vector, source, license, version, uncertainty, and sensitivity metadata.
- Relevance ranking is deterministic, explainable, and configurable; the same profile/date/pack versions/seed produce the same candidates.
- Historical context is offered as fictional authoring material, not a causal claim about real people; nothing becomes canon until accepted or explicitly auto-approved by project policy.
- The editor shows why each candidate matched, supports accept/reject/edit, records lineage, and detects stale derivations after source inputs change.
- Accepted context and derived character variables round-trip through source, RON, JSON, Bevy, and PixiJS paths.
- Offline runtime packs use only original or compatibly licensed public data with documented provenance.

name: Document mandatory public-source isolation
description:
Outcome:
Repository instructions keep Weave and its synchronized artifacts entirely self-contained within original, synthetic, and compatibly licensed public material.

Requirements:
- Add a mandatory public-source isolation policy to AGENTS.md covering repository files, task metadata, issues, pull requests, commits, examples, diagnostics, and shared output.
- Require independent first-principles specification and original or compatibly licensed fixtures.
- Require a focused public-identifier, path, and provenance scan before publishing or synchronizing authored material.
- Normalize the existing domain-module epic to self-contained public-only wording.

Acceptance criteria:
- AGENTS.md states the mandatory public-only boundary and response procedure clearly.
- The domain-module dex subtree retains its functional requirements using self-contained public provenance.
- Local task data and synchronized GitHub issues pass a focused public-text scan.
- Only AGENTS.md and dex-managed task metadata change.
result: Added the mandatory public-source isolation policy to AGENTS.md, including first-principles specification, original or compatibly licensed public inputs, pre-publication scanning, and remediation guidance. Normalized the domain-module epic to public-only wording and verified local dex records plus synchronized GitHub issues 5 and 6 with the focused public-text scan.

name: Design the community pattern-system library
description:
Requirements:
- Define a package format, metadata schema, validation rules, version compatibility, licensing fields, and discovery workflow for reusable pattern systems
- Keep third-party data separate from trusted executable code
- Provide validation and publishing commands plus at least one sample package
- Document moderation and provenance expectations

Acceptance criteria:
- A community package can be validated, installed, loaded, and referenced by a story
- Invalid or incompatible packages fail safely
- The format supports semantic data, draw methods, spreads, attribution, and versioning

name: Specify the open character profile and synthesis contract
description:
Execution: HITL methodology and schema review.

What to build:
Independently specify the public Character Profile, including stable identity fields, partial or full birth-date precision, canonical HEXACO factors/facets and bands, confidence, derived OCEAN, pluggable alignment views, authored inner-life/voice fields, source lineage, and deterministic synthesis/override rules. Separate normative data from optional display and suggestion layers.

Acceptance criteria:
- The specification defines all 24 HEXACO facets, valid band/value forms, missing-data behavior, confidence, and schema evolution.
- OCEAN derivation is documented, reproducible, labeled lossy/derived, and cannot write back or be counted as independent evidence.
- Alignment and date-context extensions declare authority, rationale, version, and provenance and cannot silently change canonical traits.
- Authored, imported, derived, suggested, reviewed, and overridden values have distinguishable states and deterministic precedence.
- Equivalent canonical RON and JSON fixtures plus invalid fixtures cover the contract.
- The specification, fixtures, and algorithms are written from first principles and are original or compatibly licensed with documented public provenance.

name: Epic: Weave Character module
description:
Outcome:
Ship an optional Weave Character module that creates coherent, author-controlled character seed data from a structured personality profile, alignment views, birth date or year, and relevant historical/date context, then exposes that data to Weave stories and game engines.

Requirements:
- Use the 24-facet HEXACO model as the canonical behavioral profile with explicit bands and confidence; provide OCEAN/Big Five as a transparent derived view so overlapping evidence is not double-counted.
- Support versioned narrative alignment systems as explainable projections or authored views, never diagnoses or hidden behavioral authority.
- Combine personality with birth date/year and selected date-in-history context through deterministic, inspectable synthesis rules and explicit authority/override policies.
- Expose identity, traits, inner-life fields, voice guidance, alignment, date context, and derivation lineage as typed variables in syntax and the editor.
- Specify every mechanic independently from first principles, using original algorithms and synthetic or compatibly licensed public inputs.

Acceptance criteria:
- A writer can create, inspect, revise, validate, compile, and consume a complete synthetic character from public inputs.
- HEXACO remains canonical, OCEAN is labeled as derived, and every alignment/date enrichment shows its source and rationale.
- Generated suggestions never silently overwrite authored canon and can be accepted, rejected, or overridden in text and editor workflows.
- Equivalent versioned RON and JSON character packs are usable from minimal Bevy and PixiJS examples.
- Public fixtures, corpora, weights, and documentation are original or compatibly licensed and safe for MIT distribution.

name: Design the PatternSystem trait and shared data model
description:
Requirements:
- Define the weave-patterns extension boundary for pattern elements, semantic fields, draws, spreads, positions, reversals, and draw methods
- Separate immutable pattern definitions from mutable draw state
- Support deterministic seeded tests and serialization through the compiler IR
- Allow built-in and user-authored systems to share runtime behavior

Acceptance criteria:
- The tarot and weather-omen examples in README.md are representable without special cases
- Trait objects or generics have a documented ownership and serialization strategy
- Invalid definitions return structured diagnostics

name: Build the example game integration
description:
Requirements:
- Create a small Bevy game that uses compiled Weave dialogue, choices, observable state, hot reload, and pattern draws
- Demonstrate UI reaction to PatternDrawn and story events
- Keep art and setup lightweight so the example remains a useful integration reference

Acceptance criteria:
- The example runs from a documented cargo command
- Automated smoke tests cover story loading and event flow
- The example is kept compatible with the supported Bevy version

name: Compose and export portable Weave World packs
description:
Execution: AFK.

What to build:
Complete Weave World by supporting deterministic composition of broad, regional, ecosystem, and authored layers, then package the resolved world and optional source lineage for use outside Weave. A writer can start broad, refine with a region or biome, and keep deliberate fictional overrides authoritative.

Acceptance criteria:
- Composition order, conflict handling, inheritance, pinned pack versions, and random-seed behavior are explicit and deterministic.
- The editor previews the resolved world, shows layer provenance and differences, and lets authors promote generated values to authored overrides.
- Compact runtime exports can omit authoring provenance while full exports retain it; both forms have versioned RON and JSON schemas.
- Minimal Bevy and PixiJS examples use world rules, place data, and environmental variables to alter game behavior or presentation.
- Golden fixtures prove equivalent semantics across source, editor, RON, JSON, and both engine consumers.
- Public sample packs and documentation remain independently authored and redistributable.

name: Specify module manifests, namespaces, and compatibility
description:
Execution: HITL architecture review.

What to build:
Specify the domain-module contract before committing to syntax or crate boundaries. Cover module identity and versions, declared capabilities, namespaced variable/object types, pack dependencies, deterministic resolution order, diagnostics, provenance, and compatibility/migration rules. Decide which extension points are declarative and whether any executable extension surface is necessary.

Acceptance criteria:
- The language and architecture documentation define module installation, imports or activation, namespace resolution, variable exposure, and failure behavior.
- Canonical RON and JSON fixtures represent the same manifest and module data without semantic loss.
- Version negotiation and forward/backward compatibility rules are explicit and tested at the schema boundary.
- The design prevents two modules from silently shadowing names or changing output based on discovery order.
- The specification and fixtures are independently written, synthetic or compatibly licensed, and include documented public provenance.

name: Epic: Pluggable domain modules
description:
Outcome:
Weave supports independently distributed domain modules that contribute typed seed data, source-language affordances, editor experiences, and runtime variables without folding every domain into the core language.

Requirements:
- Preserve text-first and visual-editor parity for every module capability.
- Use deterministic, versioned contracts for module manifests, generated variables, diagnostics, and provenance.
- Round-trip module data through human-readable RON and stable JSON, with straightforward consumption from Bevy and PixiJS projects.
- Keep module code and data packs independently composable, replaceable, and exportable.
- Specify public behavior independently from first principles.
- Admit only original, MIT-compatible, or compatibly licensed public fixtures and corpora, with machine-readable provenance.

Acceptance criteria:
- Weave World and Weave Character use the same documented extension boundary end to end.
- Installing or removing a module does not require domain-specific changes throughout Weave core.
- Source, editor, compiler, runtime, RON, JSON, Bevy, and PixiJS contract tests cover a representative module.
- Public documentation and examples are original or compatibly licensed and include required provenance.

name: Add the live play preview
description:
Requirements:
- Run the current compiled story inside the editor without restarting the app
- Display narrative lines and choices, permit selection, and expose current variables and pattern draws
- Support replay from any knot and deterministic seeded sessions
- Preserve the last valid preview when current source has compiler errors

Acceptance criteria:
- Edits trigger a debounced compile and update the preview
- Users can step, choose, restart, and jump to a knot
- Runtime and compiler failures are actionable and do not crash the editor

name: Layer world rules, named places, and local overrides
description:
Execution: AFK.

What to build:
Let an author turn a reference seed into a fictional setting by declaring world-level rules, stable named places, nested or related locations, and local environmental or climate overrides. Preserve inherited values and their lineage so authors and runtimes can distinguish sourced defaults from fictional decisions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Source syntax and editor workflows can create, rename, reorder, nest, and relate stable place identifiers without breaking references.
- Places support an extensible typed attribute map plus explicit environment/climate inheritance and overrides.
- World rules are typed, namespaced variables usable by narrative logic and exported consumers.
- The editor presents a place hierarchy and inspector that distinguish inherited, generated, and authored values and can reset an override.
- Authored source, editor state, RON, and JSON round-trip without changing identifiers or semantics.
- Optional naming data is separately packaged and licensed; the default workflow never fabricates cultural claims from a geographic preset.

name: Create the Phase 1 example stories
description:
Requirements:
- Add basic grammar and branching stories that exercise Phase 1 language features
- Add a standalone runtime example and a Bevy dialogue integration example
- Keep examples small, documented, and usable as regression fixtures
- Reserve the full fortune-teller and I-Ching showcases for pattern-system completion

Acceptance criteria:
- Every example compiles and runs in CI
- README commands point to working packages and files
- Examples demonstrate both standalone and Bevy usage without hidden setup
result: Added documented basic grammar and branching stories plus finite standalone compiler/runtime and headless Bevy asset/event packages. Both examples have smoke tests and were run successfully from their README cargo commands.

Execution: AFK.

Turn the tracer-bullet extension into a contributor-ready packaging workflow. A project can install or reference a module and its data packs, validate them before compilation, watch them during editing, and report compatibility or provenance failures without domain-specific core changes.

Acceptance criteria:

name: Implement the AST and type checker

name: Add explainable, pluggable alignment views
description:
Execution: AFK with methodology review.

What to build:
Support separately packaged narrative alignment systems that project canonical character evidence onto named axes or categories. Ship one original, public-safe example pack with transparent factors, weights, thresholds, explanations, and a review workflow; alignment remains a storytelling shorthand rather than a personality diagnosis or runtime authority.

Acceptance criteria:
- An alignment pack declares its input fields, version, scoring rules, thresholds, labels, limitations, license, and calibration fixtures.
- Deterministic proposals carry an explanation trace and cannot alter canonical HEXACO or authored canon.
- Proposed, reviewed, overridden, and withheld states are distinct; override or withholding requires a saved rationale.
- Source syntax and the editor can select a pack, inspect the proposal, review or override it, and expose only approved values to narrative logic.
- RON and JSON preserve the chosen public view while optional authoring exports retain the review trace.
- A contributor can add another alignment system through the public module/data-pack contract without changing Character core.
- Documentation clearly states the non-diagnostic, fictional-purpose boundary.
